title: Primavera
subtitle: The brilliance and hope of the renaissance.

trails.title: The Stalker
trails.description: The protagonists' adventure is over, marking the beginning of the merchant's search.

content.text:
[Southeast Corner of the Room]
Piles of a sand-quicklime mixture, a bit of carbon dust, several nails and punched paintings.
Just some leftover materials they didn't use. Worthless to me.

[East of the Room]
Two carving knives, several brushes, and a piece of glass.
Nothing worth taking.
The glass looks like some kind of lens.

Dried Paint
They didn't seal the paint can with beeswax! What a waste ...

A dozen letters and several intact paintings.
Finally, something worth taking.
I can make a new manuscript and name it Mystery of the Frescos or Wonders of Florence ... No, I need a more eye-catching title.

[North of the Room]
Scaffoldings.
Collapsed.

Messy carvings: a group of dancing human symbols, their meaning is unclear.
Is this a signature? I bet the scaffoldings were broken by the ones who were fighting.

trails.title: Corner of the Secret Chamber
trails.description: A dusty letter found inside the chamber. Part of the writing is blurred.

content.text:
Dear Uccello,
It's been too long since we parted. I heard you went back to Pratovecchio. Is it still as beautiful as you said it was? I still remember what it looked like in your painting—a sea of olive and fig trees.
Those days we spent together were just like a dream. I've always wanted to pick up the brush once again, but my life is already occupied by meaningless housework ... They said I didn't have much time left. (Blurred)

But I came back without letting anyone know. When I left a new signature at the corner, I found that our friends had done the same thing. Lippi, Giovanni ... What about you? I'm never sure since you've always been so unpredictable.

How are you doing? Hopefully, you're still drawing.
In fact, I know you are.

Bianca

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Oh, thank heavens. No more befuddling riddles and clouds of sleeping gas. I've never loved this world as much as I do now!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: You were quite clever to cooperate with Alberto to stall for time. But how did you know that Ezio was coming to save us?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I didn't know. But I knew that irritating Alberto would risk the safety of Sotheby and Leonardo.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Moreover, I think I may have actually figured out what the "relics" truly are ...
A small, brownish shadow flashes past the window.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Hmm? That sound is familiar, isn't it?

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I'll take a look.
Another clumsy little bird carrying its creator's encrypted message.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: "Sicuro." He means he's safe.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Looks like my friends from the Thieves' Guild have already rescued Leonardo and Miss Sotheby.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You seem to have a lot of friends.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I always thought that assassins worked alone.
Smiling, the Assassin shakes his head.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Quite the opposite.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: True assassins, are more than just killers. We are the manifestation of a belief. A belief in freedom and the ability to fight for it.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: We do not hold to any authority but our own. We are free to follow our own path.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: And many share that belief. That's why we are never alone.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: ... Just like the artists that painted these.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I imagine they must see each other as fellow believers in art.
For a moment, everyone takes a moment to appreciate the mottled frescoes surrounding them.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: So ... the outline of their story should be clear now.
One by one, the pages that had been scattered to an unknown corner of history fall neatly together.
They should have been carried away by the winds of time, like fallen leaves.
But if these pages were ever meant to be rediscovered someday, then yes—
Now is that moment.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: About 20 years ago, a group of painters led by Uccello started working on the fresco here.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Even today, you can still sense the enthusiasm in their work.

items.speaker: Male Painter I
items.text: The essence of linear perspective lies not only in reproducing reality, but in the narrative quality of space itself!

items.speaker: Male Painter II
items.text: You've only scratched the surface. If you truly want to grasp the essence of the concept, I suggest you review Plato's theory of forms.

items.speaker: Male Painter II
items.text: Rather than simply copying nature, as artists, we should strive to reveal their true ideals through our work.

items.speaker: Female Painter
items.text: I'm so jealous of them.

items.speaker: Female Painter
items.text: They are so talented and knowledgeable ... unlike me. I feel dizzy just seeing those guidelines.

items.speaker: Uccello
items.text: Bah, let me show you some tricks better than mere linear perspective!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Here, Uccello lifted a stained glass to showcase his wondrous optical phenomenon.

items.speaker: Male Painter I
items.text: Not again, Uccello! You can't keep altering our work with that strange pigment of yours!

items.speaker: Male Painter I
items.text: What a mess. And it goes against our patron's instructions. What if they find out about it?

items.speaker: Uccello
items.text: Hmph, look closely.

items.speaker: Male Painter II
items.text: The modified colors and lines do give the work a little more life. Fine, I admit it, you know what you're doing!

items.speaker: Male Painter III
items.text: He's right. I say we keep it—it's not like our patrons are ever smart enough to figure these things out anyway ...

items.speaker: Female Painter
items.text: It never occurred to me painting could be so ... liberating. Thank you for enlightening me.

items.speaker: Uccello
items.text: Huh? Of course, to paint is to find freedom. That is what it always has been!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It was a time of joy and of meaningful creation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But it didn't last long.

items.speaker: Guild Official
items.text: I'm sorry we must suspend funding for now; there is simply no money to pay you.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: All at once, the painters and artisans were kicked out of the cathedral.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Stripped of their right to finish their final painting, leaving no room for negotiation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No payments, and no written records were left behind.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: But life had to go on. These painters and artisans scattered each one doing what they could to earn their bread.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: But always returning to the unfinished fresco that tugged at their heartstrings.

items.speaker: Female Painter
items.text: That night, I returned to the dome. But I never expected to find Uccello there as well.

items.speaker: Female Painter
items.text: Then others came ... one by one.

items.speaker: Female Painter
items.text: Turns out, I wasn't the only one reluctant to leave our work behind.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Again, Uccello lifted the stained glass and—

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Their story has come to a pause here. Now, let's finish it ...
He lifts APPLe gently into the light, it reflects off his golden radiance as the Assassin walks toward the unfinished fresco.
